revisionReason: Round 1 and the first adversarial audit proved that a reachable commit and one browser test were not enough. This revision narrows the claim to a source/runtime byte checkpoint and adds independent recovery, fresh deployment, normal-flow, cache-body, evidence-integrity, and canonical-document requirements before Round 2 may pass.
scope: recover the exact V0.8.2 source, deployment inputs, runtime assets, and license bytes
run the recovered runtime through deterministic and normal-player browser paths
prove a fresh Vercel build can be made from the exact baseline tree
record the historical deployment separately from the current fixed Production target
preserve raw, visual, repository, deployment, and browser evidence for later recalculation
document every legacy limitation without treating the baseline as the target product

separateCapabilities.reason: V0.8.2 stores data only in browser localStorage and has no export, server backup, or recovery source for deleted or irrecoverably corrupted user data. Step 1A must not claim otherwise.
Emulated Chromium/WebKit evidence is not physical-device evidence. Physical iPhone approval remains mandatory at the later product QA gate.

The public Production runtime was healthy and byte-identical. A real alias switch is an externally visible operation and is not required to prove the source/runtime checkpoint; the promote and roll-forward runbook is documented instead.

requirements.condition: The baseline commit and tree resolve exactly, git fsck passes, and the baseline uses neither Git LFS nor submodules.
GitHub retains an archive branch at the exact baseline commit and the review branch contains a self-contained, SHA-256-bound runtime snapshot independent of that mutable archive ref.
The runtime manifest contains all 17 served execution/license paths and also binds .vercelignore and vercel.json.
A clean GitHub checkout of the archive branch passes the current independent verification kit through CATS_BASELINE_DIR.
The historical baseline Vercel deployment is READY and reports the baseline commit.
The historical deployment, current fixed Production deployment, and fresh recovery deployment are three separately named identities.
All 17 fixed-Production manifest paths have the expected status, MIME type, byte length, and SHA-256.

Vercel freshly builds a no-content commit whose tree is exactly the baseline tree; all 15 non-HTML entries match directly and both HTML paths match after removal of only the official Preview Toolbar injection.
The recovered runtime completes the existing 1F-through-10F deterministic loop at 390x844 and 375x667.
Without qa=1 and with normal motion, a player can start, enter real battle, and reload successfully at both mobile viewports.
With service workers enabled, the test verifies controller acquisition, every cached response body SHA-256, obsolete and synthetic future cache removal, and offline shell restart.
Schema-2 durable state reloads and the raw future-schema localStorage string remains byte-for-byte unmodified.
Mid-combat roster non-persistence, unavailable deleted-save recovery, and the physical-device evidence boundary are stated as limitations.
Every raw report and final-size visual has a stored artifact and a verifier-checked SHA-256.
Three independent critics and a final judge re-audit the strengthened artifact after CI; every material finding is resolved or explicitly outside the narrowed scope.
No original game runtime, asset, PWA, or deployment-input file changes during the Step 1 redo.
README, AGENTS, MASTER_SPEC, FLOORS_1_10_DESIGN, PROJECT_HANDOVER, PROJECT_STATUS, and BASELINE_V082 agree on Step 1 and the revalidation state of later steps.
The strengthened Acceptance is committed before the final review; Round 2 binds that commit and the verifier rejects later Acceptance edits.

automaticFailureConditions: Step 1 is described without the source/runtime scope qualifier
a mutable remote ref is the only retained copy
the recovery test depends on files that do not exist in the selected recovery checkout without explaining the separate validation kit
Vercel READY is used as the only deployment evidence
the current fixed alias is falsely described as the historical baseline deployment
a fresh build has a different Git tree from the baseline
normal UI or service-worker-enabled paths are absent
cache names are checked without hashing cached response bodies
future-schema preservation is tested only as parsed JSON rather than the raw stored string
raw reports or final-size visual evidence are missing
physical iPhone, player-save backup, or an actual Production alias switch is claimed without evidence
an original runtime or deployment-input byte changes
the final PASS changes or weakens this Acceptance after its committed checkpoint
any independent critic or final judge has an unresolved material blocker
